title: Juz' 'Amma, the shape
hookLine: thirty-seven surahs: the Day, the orphan, the soul, the One

cards: Near the top of a hike, there's a moment when you turn around.
The path you climbed is laid out below you, and for the first time you can see its shape: where it switched back, where it got steep, where you stopped for water.

Since day one hundred fifty-nine, this path has walked backward through the last part of the Qur'an, from An-Nas on its final page to An-Naba' at the front. Yesterday it reached the start. So today, no new surah.
Just a turn around, to look at the whole thing: thirty-seven surahs, and four things they keep coming back to.

teach.b: Juz' means a part. The Qur'an's surahs are of very different lengths, so later Muslims divided the text into thirty parts of roughly equal length, to be read in a month, a part a day, as some do in Ramadan.
The division is a reading aid, not part of the revelation itself.
The thirtieth part runs from Surah seventy-eight to the end, thirty-seven surahs, named for its first word, 'amma, about what.
They're short, they rhyme, and several open with oaths: by the dawn, by the sun, by the fig and the olive. Under all that sound, four themes keep returning.
The Day: An-Naba', Az-Zalzalah, Al-Qari'ah, the sorting and the weighing.

teach.h: THE DAY, THE ORPHAN, THE SOUL, THE ONE.
teach.b: The orphan: again and again the surahs ask who fed the orphan and who pushed him away, from Ad-Duha to Al-Ma'un.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came from an orphan's childhood himself, which gives those verses a sound all their own. The soul: Ash-Shams swears by the soul and the One who shaped it, and says whoever purifies it has succeeded.
And the One: Al-Ikhlas, four short lines on the oneness of Allah. It's often the first part children learn by heart: short enough to hold, one surah at a time, and full of those four things.

how: Muslim children often learn Juz' 'Amma first, starting from its end (An-Nas) and working backward, and its short surahs are commonly recited in the daily prayers; the thirty-part division lets a reader finish the whole Qur'an across a month, as some do in Ramadan.

games.why: the thirty parts of roughly equal length make a month's reading, a part a day.

practice: Let the last few weeks come back one surah at a time: the whisperer that withdraws, daybreak, Say, He is Allah, the One, the morning light of Ad-Duha, the man who frowned, the trumpet and the crowds.
Don't try to remember them all; notice which ones come back on their own. Hold three of their names, and ask what each one gave you.
